raw.assessment: The incumbent supplies removable partitions already assembled and checks an order slip, providing an opportunity to verify the requested configuration. Repeated three-compartment orders approach the time target (D2-O6), so assembly is not uniformly slow. Mixed batches contain every extreme delay, but layout complexity and switching are confounded. Missing/incorrect-part reports and unpacking confusion show checks and the generic diagram do not reliably secure the outcome (D2-O3/O4). Concrete limitation: insertion-retry widths overlap first-pass widths (D2-O5), weakening a simple width-only account without excluding slot fit, orientation or handling. These are synthetic observations, not established causal explanations.

openings.claim: Preparing an order-specific parts set and checking it against the selected layout before insertion may reduce mixed-batch selection mistakes and delays.
openings.delta: Replace repeated shared-bin selection during assembly with a bounded per-order selection and verification step; retain full assembly and reversible joints.
openings.prediction: Within the same layout and worker, prepared sets reduce selection/checking time or detected component discrepancies; insertion time may remain unchanged. Unchanged selection performance would weaken this account.
openings.probe: Use spare-board samples in counterbalanced matched runs, recording selection, insertion, checking and packing separately. Include set preparation in total time and inspect final parts/count/color. Gate adoption on measured cost limits and available time before the fixed delivery date.
assumptions: Layout-specific required parts can be derived from existing templates and order slips.
Preparation does not consume more time or bench capacity than it saves; cost and schedule feasibility remain unmeasured.

openings.claim: A diagram of the customer's ordered layout explicitly locating the short partition may improve unaided arrangement.
openings.delta: Replace the three-layout diagram with order-specific placement guidance, without changing components or rearrangeability.
openings.prediction: Customers receiving the specific diagram make fewer short-partition placement errors and achieve their ordered layout more often; persistent failures suggest guidance alone is insufficient.
openings.probe: Assign the ten willing participants across existing versus specific diagrams, balancing layout and prior exposure. Verify complete kits beforehand; record unaided success and placement errors. Treat this small comparison as directional evidence; verify production outcomes in the 60-unit pilot.
assumptions: Diagram preparation and printing fit both cost caps and the fixed deadline.
Previously observed participants may have learned the layouts, limiting generalization.

raw.assessment: Synthetic observations support investigating selection and arrangement ambiguity, but do not establish the source of missing parts or insertion retries. This proposed hybrid remains unvalidated against time, cost, delivery, capacity and customer-success requirements.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: an order-specific reusable packing map can carry each supplied partition in a labeled outline and then unfold beside the base as an assembly guide. This moves inventory checking and short-part placement guidance into the shipping artifact, permitting customer assembly while retaining removable partitions.
openings.delta: Parent mechanisms are a physical inventory silhouette and a spatial assembly template. Their interaction makes each carried part correspond to its destination in the selected arrangement. Mixed-layout complexity becomes information: an unmatched outline or leftover part exposes a discrepancy. A speculative extension would prevent the carrier closing unless every required part occupies its matching position; dependencies include shape discrimination, reversible retention and a closure that cannot be defeated by an empty pocket. The presently testable partial capability is visible mismatch detection using hand-cut or drawn maps.
openings.prediction: Compared with the incumbent diagram, mapped kits should reduce short-part placement questions and expose planted missing or wrong partitions before dispatch. Workshop time should fall only if map preparation, loading and checking cost less time than the removed assembly.
openings.probe: Use spare board to prototype maps for the three accepted compartment counts. Test detectable omissions and substitutions with both workers, separately timing selection, loading, checking and packing. Assign ten participants to mapped kits or incumbent presentation using comparable layouts; record unaided arrangement, questions and completion. Check capacity, rearrangement, color, actual material costs and preparation time before committing the fixed-date pilot. Pilot targets remain at least 59 complete orders, median workshop time at most eight minutes and at least 54 unaided customer arrangements.
assumptions: Existing packaging can be adapted within 500 initial and 0.40 recurring cost limits.
Map production fits the existing delivery schedule.
Failure boundary: visually similar wrong parts, incorrect maps or loose contents can defeat the visible check; closure interlocking is speculative.

critiques.assumption: Agreement between parts, packing map and destination diagram establishes agreement with the accepted order.
critiques.limitation: A wrong map could accept a complete set for another layout and teach that same wrong arrangement. D2-O3/O4 establish discrepancies and confusion, but do not establish this common-source failure. Geometric outlines also need not distinguish exterior color.
critiques.opening: Check order identity independently before using the map to check physical completeness and guide placement.
critiques.comparison: The inventory silhouette detects absent or mismatched shapes; the spatial template explains destinations. Their coupling transfers one correspondence from packing to assembly, but also propagates a wrong correspondence. Z1 and Z2 can share this vulnerability if both inherit the same mistaken layout selection. A closure interlock adds physical occupancy enforcement but cannot establish that the map represents the accepted order.
critiques.probe: Deliberately swap otherwise complete layout maps between sample orders, including the same layout with a wrong exterior color. Compare shape-only checks with independent order-slip checks; these are proposed challenges, not observed failures.

openings.claim: An independently verified order-specific map may combine inventory checking and placement guidance while catching configurations that are internally consistent but wrong for the order.
openings.delta: Before loading, the second worker checks the map against the original order slip for compartment count, component requirements and exterior color; the packing worker then checks physical contents against the verified map. Both checking times count toward workshop time.
openings.prediction: Relative to A1, this should detect more swapped-map errors; relative to Z1, the retained map should help placement; relative to Z2, physical matching should expose omissions. Shared mistaken specifications or rushed second checks defeat the interaction.
openings.probe: Reuse up to 15 samples across counterbalanced challenged checks by both workers. Include map preparation and both checks in total time. Use ten participants for directional unaided-arrangement evidence. Measure actual costs and delivery feasibility before adoption; only the 60-order pilot can assess its specified completeness, time and customer-success targets.
assumptions: Original slips accurately preserve accepted choices.
Independent checking remains practical with two workers and one bench.
The unchanged footprint, stationery capacity, removable partitions, accepted counts/colors, cost caps and delivery date remain mandatory.

openings.claim: Prepare and verify order-specific parts sets; retain workshop assembly.
openings.discriminator: Selection/checking improves within worker/layout; insertion may not.
openings.probe: Counterbalance matched runs; time preparation, selection, insertion, checking and packing; inspect contents/color.
openings.uncertainty: Switching and complexity confounded; bench/time savings unknown. Overlapping widths leave insertion cause unresolved.

openings.claim: Supply the ordered-layout diagram locating the short partition.
openings.discriminator: Fewer placement errors with complete kits isolates guidance benefit.
openings.probe: Compare diagrams with ten participants, balancing layout/exposure; record unaided success.
openings.uncertainty: Small, potentially practiced sample; preparation/printing feasibility unknown.

openings.claim: A reusable map carries partitions in outlines corresponding to assembly destinations; a second worker independently verifies count, components and color against the original order before loading.
openings.discriminator: Physical matching detects omissions; destinations guide assembly; independent verification detects internally consistent wrong orders.
openings.probe: Reuse up to 15 samples: plant omissions, substitutions, swapped maps and wrong colors; compare shape-only versus independent checks. Time map preparation/loading/both checks/packing; compare customer assembly using ten participants.
openings.uncertainty: Slips may be wrong; similar parts, loose contents, rushed checks or damage defeat benefit. Closure interlock parked as speculative; occupancy cannot verify order identity.

lineage.reason: Merged with Q1; preserve carrier/template interaction and park interlock.
Merged with A1; retain independent identity check and comparison.

post_distill.decision: Probe only; synthetic evidence establishes no mechanism. Gate adoption on 30x20 cm footprint, same stationery capacity, removable partitions, accepted counts/colors, <=500 initial and <=0.40/order materials, fixed delivery. Check damage and rearrangement. Pilot requires >=59/60 complete orders, median workshop time <=8 minutes, >=54/60 unaided arrangements.
